question: Should OpenClaw expose a plugin-visible skill install/update completion observer, and what redacted payload plus observer-failure semantics should it use?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing lifecycle surface, but deciding what install metadata plugins may observe and whether observer failures affect an already-written install is a security and product boundary choice.

options.title: Add Minimal Observer
options.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, target, provenance, outcome, and timestamp metadata plus documented fail-open logging semantics.

options.title: Keep Pre-Install Only
options.body: Declare `security.installPolicy` and `before_install` sufficient for install security and explicitly narrow or reject the audit-observer portion of this issue.

options.title: Defer To ClawHub Trust Design
options.body: Hold the observer until maintainers define a broader ClawHub trust/provenance API that can supply the same audit events safely.

recommendation.title: Add Minimal Observer
recommendation.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, target, provenance, outcome, and timestamp metadata plus documented fail-open logging semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses ClawHub skill install behavior and public plugin lifecycle API shape, and steipete is the strongest product-routing signal from discussion and file history.
